# In-Context Learning and Tool-Based Control

[Home](../../../../README.md) · [All categories](../../../README.md) · [简体中文](in-context-tool-control_cn.md)

Manipulation Action Models → Gripper Manipulation Models → Agent Architectures → In-Context Learning and Tool-Based Control

Agent architectures that use demonstrations, goals and interaction history as context to select parameterized robot-tool actions. Specify context construction, fixed versus updated weights, motion execution and returned feedback; distinguish numerical tool control from a learned WAM executor.

| [AM.MAN.GRIP.AGENT.ICL.1] <a id="am-man-grip-agent-icl-1"></a> | **GPT-Policy｜VLM Agent · In-context learning · Closed-loop tool control**<br>[In-Context Robot Learning with VLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.19138v1)<br>Dongzhou Cheng, Taoran Yi et al<br>**Tags:** `gripper` `bimanual` `agent-architecture` `vlm` `in-context-learning` `tool-use` `video-demonstration` `goal-image` `interaction-history` `execution-feedback` `inverse-kinematics` `real-world` | GPT-Policy organizes demonstration keyframes, optional aligned action records, goal images and interaction history as context for an off-the-shelf VLM with no additional training; the VLM calls tools specifying end-effector poses and gripper commands, a motion execution layer converts these into joint trajectories, and observations and execution results update the context for online adaptation.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Studies five context families: human videos, robot videos with actions, goal images, self-interaction history and online human interaction, across cloth/notebook pickup, bottle opening, plug manipulation, arrangement and mobile exploration. YAM, ARX X5 and Morphi Kino dual-arm gripper configurations are documented, without establishing full task coverage on every platform. Each experimental condition has three trials; some model comparisons are individual runs and task progress is not success rate. VLM weights stay fixed and feedback updates context. Interpolation, IK and time parameterization execute motions; they do not establish collision-free or reliable contact control. Inter-arm collisions and execution/outcome-verification failures are reported. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.19138v1) · [Project](https://cheng-haha.github.io/GPT-Policy/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-24 |
